City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
May 21, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:01 p.m. , on May 21, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on May 16, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury
Absent:
Council Member Kelley
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Ury
INVOCATION: Council Member Schlicht
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Labor Negotiations - The City Council will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations are the City and the City's Unrepresented Employees. The City's Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.
CS2.
Conference With Legal Counsel-Anticipated Litigation: Initiation of Litigation pursuant to Subdivision (c) of section 54956.9 (one case).
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m., with four City Council Members present (Council Member Kelley was absent.)
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council took the Closed Session agenda items out of order and addressed item CS2 (CS1 was not heard.) The Council received information on the matter and staff will report back at next meeting with further analysis. Item CS1 was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
School Crossing Guard of Excellence
Mayor Ury presented a certificate of commendation to Joyce Brown.
P2.
Recognize Staff and Students from the Saddleback College Theater Arts Entertainment & Theater Technology Department for their Collaboration and Creation of Set Designs for Signature City Events
Mayor Ury presented certificates of appreciation to Department Chair Kent McFann, Associate Professor Karen McNulty, and students, Kathryn Bausch, Austin Burkett, Diana Campos, Lucy Darby, Zack Lapinski, Heather McLain, Danni Rodriguez, and Sarah Winfrey.
P3.
Library Card Design Contest Winners
Mayor Ury presented certificates of commendation to Mia Ross, Nathan Farlow, Alaina Klaes, Lindsey Dobrowolski, Lauren Bauer, and Julia Moynihan.
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Julie Tully, M.V.: expressed concern about the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station and stated that a nuclear disaster will affect millions. She noted that the station has broken parts and no answers and it puts the public in great danger.
Joe Tully, M.V.: implored the City Council to consider all of the safety issues with the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station. He further commented on the UDR low income housing requirement, noting that he is happy that a compromise was achieved but he feels some Council Members failed the community by not supporting it.
Gary Headrick, San Clemente: announced that there are individuals working at San Onofre who are afraid to report problems for fear of retaliation. He asked the Council to place an item on a future agenda so interested parties can speak in depth on the matter. Torgen Johnson, Solana Beach: provided information and a PowerPoint presentation on nuclear power dangers. He discussed public safety issues with the San Onofre station in the event of a major earthquake which is expected to occur within the next 30 years. Jenifer Massey, San Clemente: stated that Fukushima was a wakeup call to many and she echoed that a major earthquake in Southern California is inevitable. An earthquake above 7.0 would compromise SONGS and put Southern California residents in danger.
Dan Farrell, San Juan Capistrano: expressed concern about SONGS and public safety. He urged the Council to add an item to a future agenda in order to take a more thorough look at safety issues.
Donna Gilmore, San Clemente: stated that San Onofre employees were being punished for reporting safety violations. She stated that SONGS, of all nuclear plants in the nation, has the worst record, the highest rate of safety allegations, and the highest rate of fear of retaliation. She invited the Council and residents to visit www.sanonofresafety.org for more information.
Sharon Hoffman, Carlsbad: stated that San Onofre is a problem for residents from San Diego to Los Angeles. Nuclear power has the ability to damage all people, especially infants, children, women, and those with a compromised immune system. Ms. Hoffman urged the Council to put an item on a future agenda so that her group can provide more detailed information.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items 3 and 8 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Kelley
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further reading waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 7, 2012, as amended. The Minutes were corrected to reflect that Larry Gilbert spoke in favor of the proposal for agenda item 9 (page 4.)
4.
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer's Monthly Report for March 2012
Received and filed.
5.
Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for March 2012
Received and filed.
6.
Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer's Monthly Report for March 2012
Received and filed.
7.
Quarterly Check Registers and Quarterly Cash Receipts Report - Third Quarter of FY 2011-12
Received and filed.
9.
Quarterly Financial Report for the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency - Third Quarter of 2011-12
Received and filed.
10.
Check Register dated April 27, 2012 in the amount of $532,432.70
Ratified the accompanying check register.
11.
Check Register dated May 4, 2012 in the amount of $870,071.19
Ratified the accompanying check register.
12.
Reissuance of the Variance to Municipal Code 97-169 for Casta del Sol Homeowners Association
Authorized staff to reissue the variance to the Casta del Sol Homeowners Association for Municipal Code Firearm Ordinance 97-169.
13.
Reissuance of the Variance to Municipal Code 97-169 for Palmia Homeowners Association
Authorized staff to reissue the variance to the Palmia Homeowners Association for Municipal Code Firearm Ordinance 97-169.
14.
Annual Review of Residential and Commercial Integrated Waste Management Rates
Adopted Resolution 12-27 Approving the Proposed Contractually Based CPI Trash Rate Adjustments for Residential (2.45% Increase from $12.11 to $12.40 per Month), Commercial (2.52% Increase), and Roll-Off (1.17% Increase) Services, and Transfer and Disposal of Waste Delivered to Southeast Resource Recovery Facility (3.8% Increase) Effective July 1, 2012.
15.
Agreement to Purchase Upgrade to Library Automated System Software and Hardware Support
(1) Approved two contracts with SirsiDynix Inc, one contract in an amount not to exceed $133,301 for automation related software, hardware, and services at the Mission Viejo Library, and the second contract for the maintenance for the remaining four years of the agreement in an amount not to exceed $228,030; and (2) authorized the Mayor to execute the contract pending submittal of all required contract documents.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
OLD BUSINESS
16.
Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Director of Recreation and Community Services Kelly Doyle presented the staff report.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Ury, to approve Change Order No.10 to the Construction Contract with Western Alta Construction Company in an amount $11,809 for the project.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
Council Member Kelley
17.
Landscape Improvements to the Marguerite Tennis Center
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services, presented the staff report.
Council Member Schlicht indicated that she will not approve any additional spending for this project. She feels like the Council has been had and the citizens have not been delivered what they were promised.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) approve a Maintenance Contract Amendment with Spectrum Care Landscape and Irrigation and (2) adopt Resolution 12-28 Amending the Budget for Costs Related to the Marguerite Tennis Center Capital Improvement Project (CIP 501.)
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
Council Member Schlicht
ABSENT:
Council Member Kelley
NEW BUSINESS
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
3.
City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for March 2012
Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.
Council Member Schlicht stated that she is interested in learning more about governmental accounting and she asked for clarification on the City’s discretionary reserves.
Motion made by Council Member Leckness, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to received and file.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Kelley
8.
Quarterly Financial Report for the City of Mission Viejo - Third Quarter of 2011-12
By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.
MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS
18.
Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: announced that the OCFA Board has directed their staff to investigate disability filings and the possibility of disability fraud.
Council Member Kelley was absent therefore the OCFA report was continued to the next City Council Meeting.
19.
Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the Foothill/Eastern TCA.
20.
San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San Joaquin Hills TCA.
STAFF REPORTS
City Manager's Report
City Attorney's Report
COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS
21.
Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended
The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht announced that she spent a few minutes in the civic center courtyard before the meeting to view the American Heroes Tribute banners. She invited residents to walk among the banners and read about the soldiers who gave it all to help make America what it is. She announced that this year’s Memorial Day service will be held at 8:30 a.m. on May 28 and she invited residents to attend. Council Member Schlicht observed that the U.S. soldiers who gave their lives are the largest holders of America’s debt.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she regrets that she will not be able to attend the Memorial Day event this year as she will be out of state. She discussed the American Heroes tribute and she encouraged residents to bring their children to see the banners so they can read some of the stories of the men and women who gave their lives for this country. She also outlined her attendance at the recent Job Fair and thanked Karen Wylie for her efforts with the event. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon stated that Mission Viejo is having a problem with accidental prescription drug overdose deaths and there have been seventeen deaths in the last five years. She encouraged residents to see the documentary movie “Overtaken” which will screen at Kaleidoscope center on June 7, 2012, from 6:30 to 8:00 p.m. It will also be shown on Mission Viejo Television, Channel 30, airing every night at 9:00 p.m. for the next few weeks. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon read a very moving letter from the mother of a heroin addict and she encouraged parents to go out and see Overtaken and become informed about this very serious problem. Finally, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon wished her colleagues a very nice Memorial Day and she encouraged everyone to be thankful for all that our troops have done for us. She also thanked City staff for working hard and for doing a very fine job.
Mayor Ury
Mayor Ury announced that he gave opening remarks at the Orange County Triathlon and he thanked Council Member Leckness for the invitation. Mayor Ury encouraged residents to attend the Memorial Day ceremony, noting that it puts things into perspective as one considers those who gave the full measure of devotion.
ADJOURNMENT
At the hour of 7:37 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting in memory of Tom Fuentes to Monday, June 4, 2012, at 5:00 p.m.
______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk
Approved at the meeting of June 04, 2012
